title: Home
heading: One carrier. Three protocols.
text: OP_RETURN is a Bitcoin output that can never be spent. Three separate protocols write into that channel and behave differently once they land.

title: Home

text: One Bitcoin output type and three independent protocols that share it: OP-20 tokens, OP Names and OP Inscriptions.

title: Carrier
heading: Output anatomy
text: An OP_RETURN output has a value of zero and a scriptPubKey beginning 0x6a followed by data pushes. The payload is every push concatenated in order.

title: Carrier
heading: Provably unspendable
text: OP_RETURN marks the transaction invalid immediately, so no witness, signature or future soft fork can spend the output. Value sent to it is destroyed.

title: Carrier
heading: Prunable from the UTXO set
text: Because the output can never be spent, nodes skip it when building the UTXO set. Indexers must replay blocks instead of reading protocol state from UTXOs.

title: Carrier
heading: Relay and standardness
text: The long standing default data carrier limit was 83 bytes for the whole scriptPubKey with one carrier output per transaction. Bitcoin Core 30 removed that default cap. Relay policy is not consensus.

title: Carrier
heading: What it costs
text: OP_RETURN bytes are non witness data charged at four weight units per byte with no discount. Sizes for common payloads are tabulated.

title: Carrier
heading: Compared with other carriers
text: OP_RETURN against witness envelopes and against data encoded in unprunable spendable outputs, compared on where bytes live, UTXO impact, fee treatment and reveal timing.

title: Carrier
heading: Pitfalls
text: Sending value to the data output, using two data outputs, assuming the payload proves ownership, and spending an asset bearing UTXO as change.

title: Specification
heading: Conventions
text: Rejected means the reader refuses to apply the payload, never that the Bitcoin transaction is invalid. Reason codes protocol_mismatch and upstream_schema.

title: Specification

text: Ten rules covering the OP_RETURN opcode, push encodings, payload assembly, non push opcodes, truncated pushes, the 4096 byte bound, strict UTF-8, zero value and relay guidance.

title: Reference
heading: Indexer semantics
text: Confirmation minimums, mempool coverage and reorganisation handling stated separately for OP-20, OP Names and OP Inscriptions, plus the recorded sources of truth.

title: Reference
heading: Fee and size
text: No witness discount, the 83 byte relay target, dust thresholds for the receipt output, and the fact that a rejected payload costs the same fee.

title: Reference
heading: Funding safety
text: Core screens funding candidates against its own OP-20 records using batched lookups, keys a record with no output index by bare transaction id, and fails closed when the screen cannot be read.

title: Reference
heading: Security considerations
text: Interpretation is not consensus, payload addresses are not authority, retired mutation paths fail closed, homograph names, duplicate JSON keys, visible coercions and operator handled deep reorgs.

title: Reference
heading: Limitations
text: No mempool feed, no enforced freshness contract, no OP-20 or OP Names marketplace execution, no atomic listing update, no offer workflow, and the OP Names authority is not production enabled.

title: Test vectors
heading: OP-20, accepted
text: Deploy, mint, transfer with and without add, mixed case ticker, trailing bytes and a zero fraction amount, each with real script hex.

title: Test vectors
heading: OP-20, rejected
text: Two carriers, unknown field, unsupported operation, zero amount, non zero fraction and a duplicate key, with the exact rejection each produced.

title: Test vectors
heading: OP-20, not claimed
text: Foreign protocol tag, leading text, a non push opcode, a truncated pushdata and an ordinary output all return null rather than a rejection.

title: Test vectors
heading: OP Names, accepted
text: JSON registration with and without add, JSON transfer, legacy plain text and case normalisation, with the resulting identity and asset id.

title: Test vectors
heading: OP Names, recorded as evidence
text: Bad namespace, empty label, unknown field, unsupported operation, invalid UTF-8 and two carriers, each stored with a reason and never applied.

title: Test vectors
heading: OP Names, not claimed
text: Two dots, a Unicode dot lookalike and text with no dot are not claimed at all, which is the homograph defence working.

title: Test vectors
heading: Receipt selection
text: Verified outcomes for which output becomes the owner when a registration has no add field.

title: Test vectors
heading: OP Inscriptions classification
text: Explicit tag, historical envelope, foreign OP-20 and OP Names labels, plain text and arbitrary JSON as classified by the record decoder.

title: Decoder
heading: OP_RETURN decoder
text: Paste a scriptPubKey hex. The decoder lays out the bytes, identifies which protocol claims the payload, decodes fields and reports size and relay implications. Nothing leaves the page.

title: Decoder
heading: What the decoder checks
text: Carrier, then OP-20, then OP Names, then OP Inscriptions, then size and relay. It reads one output and does not resolve state.
